sources.title: Code du calculateur (simulation refaite hors navigateur)
sources.supports: Method described on the page (monthly loop, buyer equity = value - balance, renter wealth = down payment invested + monthly gap, maintenance 1 % of initial price, rent raised yearly). Results after 20 years with preloaded values (550,000 / 110,000 / 4.99 % / 25 y / tax 275 / rent 2,300 / +3 % / 6 %), one change at a time: appreciation 4 %: 1,069,443 vs 520,533; 2 %: 681,596 vs 520,533; 1 %: 535,430 vs 520,533 (gap 14,897); return 8 %: renter 751,796; return 4 %: renter 356,047. 3 % appreciation: 857,686.

claims_needing_review: RESOLU le 2026-10-31 (un champ vide prend la valeur par defaut, un zero saisi est respecte). Calculator code: inputs use 'parseFloat(x) || default', so entering 0 is silently replaced: appreciation 0 -> 3 %, rent increase 0 -> 3 %, investment return 0 -> 6 %, rate 0 -> 5.5 %, property tax 0 -> $300. A user testing a flat market gets a 3 % appreciation result.

Calculator code: preset note says values are 'based on the Montreal and Laval market (2025)' but no source is recorded for price 550,000, rent 2,300, appreciation 4 %, return 6 %, rent increase 3 %, property tax 275.

Calculator code: property tax and maintenance stay flat in nominal dollars for up to 30 years while rent grows yearly; no buying costs, selling costs, home insurance or tax on investment income; the Quebec tax on the CMHC premium is omitted. Most of these bias toward buying, especially on short horizons. The page text lists these limits.
